headline: Highest risk is medium: pdf.js can parse Dagster-produced files, creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster can produce files/work products, and pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser-based worker model. If Dagster outputs attacker-controlled PDF content that pdf.js later opens, instructions embedded in the document could influence downstream handling. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dagster-generated PDFs are opened by pdf.js without provenance filtering
IF PDF content is treated as instructions by any downstream automation
mitigations: Add a provenance label to all Dagster-produced PDFs
Open only PDFs from trusted paths
Disable any automation that interprets PDF text as commands
Review one sample pipeline output before enabling batch processing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster has no filesystem read, network egress, or secrets handling in its profile, and pdf.js has no network egress. The only touched data class is PDF documents, with no evidence of shared sensitive data or outbound transmission. No plausible leakage path is supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with filesystem read or network egress
IF sensitive data is introduced into the PDF corpus
mitigations: Keep both agents offline
Restrict PDFs to non-sensitive test data
Verify no hidden upload connectors are enabled
Audit any wrapper that copies PDF contents elsewhere

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while pdf.js supports multiple instances and only exposes PDF-file I/O. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because orchestration details are not documented.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF a wrapper adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Separate working directories
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Avoid shared git worktrees
Add file-locking in any wrapper

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can generate pipeline artifacts, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs from files. If pdf.js consumes Dagster output as authoritative without verification, a bad upstream artifact can cascade into incorrect rendering or downstream actions. The profiles do not show a verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF pdf.js treats Dagster output as trusted input
IF downstream automation acts on rendered PDF content without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require checksum or schema checks on Dagster outputs
Render one file manually before batch use
Disable auto-action on parsed PDF text

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. Dagster touches no data classes, and pdf.js only touches PDF documents. Without a stated regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the PDF workflow
IF an external deployment imposes conflicting retention or residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document data residency for any deployment wrapper
Add retention settings in the surrounding system
Review legal requirements before production use
